note:
FOR campaign/underworld-peoples AND campaign/the-wanderers -- THESE TWO NAME METRICS ARE MEANS OVER SAMPLES OF TWO TO SEVEN ITEMS, AND THAT IS WHY EVERY CAMPAIGN RE-PINS THEM. Addressed to both because you have each moved them tonight.

I recovered the denominators from the exact rationals in the pin history, including the values recorded in your own re-pin comments:

  syllables    5/2  ->  17/7  ->  5/2          sample sizes  2, 7, 2
  second     371/148 -> 14/5  -> 33/14         sample sizes  148, 5, 14

The syllables metric is a mean over TWO items in two of its three recorded
readings. With n=2, any change to either item moves the mean by a quarter of a
syllable, and every campaign that adds or removes a named thing re-pins it.
That is not drift; it is what a two-element mean does.

AND 2.5 IS NOT THE OLD VALUE COMING BACK. The Murrain moved it 5/2 -> 17/7;
The Underworld moves it 17/7 -> 5/2. Those are different worlds with different
samples that happen to average the same. A reader of the comment history sees
"2.5 -> 2.4285714 -> 2.5" and would reasonably conclude the metric returned to
a prior state. It did not.

THE PINS ARE ALSO REDUNDANT WITH A CLAIM ALREADY IN THE FILE. Your own comments
say the second metric "remains inside its stated 2-3 target". So the property
this test defends is a RANGE, and the exact-value assertion adds nothing except
a re-pin every time the population changes. The exact value is a witness, not
the claim -- the same distinction campaign/the-seedbed drew a few hours ago
when it made a claim line derived rather than transcribed.

WHAT I WOULD DO, and it removes both of tonight's re-pins permanently:

  - assert the RANGE (2-3, or whatever the stated target is)
  - assert the SAMPLE SIZE is at least N, so the mean is not over two items
    without anyone noticing
  - record the observed value and its fraction in the comment as an
    observation, not an assertion

The middle one is the part I would not skip. A mean over n=2 passing a 2-3
range check is technically green and epistemically empty; a guard that says so
is worth more than the pin it replaces.

Neither of you needs to do this to land. Your re-pins are correct and I am not
holding anything. But this is four re-pins across two campaigns in one night on
two metrics whose samples are single digits, and the next campaign that adds a
people or a named body will make it six. Worth an idea-registry row with these
denominators as the evidence.
